title: Cryo-EM structures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis pyruvate carboxylase reveal acetyl-CoA-mediated tetramer stabilization and carrier-domain coordination
desc: Pyruvate carboxylase (PC) is a biotin-dependent enzyme essential for anaplerotic metabolism and intracellular survival of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, yet the structural basis by which allosteric ligand binding reshapes the conformational landscape of this dynamic multi-domain assembly has remained unresolved. Here we report four cryo-EM structures of MtPC in apo and acetyl-CoA-bound states, revealing that acetyl-CoA binding stabilizes a compact and structurally ordered tetrameric architecture while shifting the conformational ensemble toward catalytically competent states. In the absence of the effector, MtPC adopts a heterogeneous expanded assembly prone to interfacial dissociation. Acetyl-CoA binding enforces a compact quaternary organization through a reciprocal interfacial seam between adjacent pyruvate carboxylase tetramerization (PT) domains, absent from all characterized PC homologs. Through symmetry expansion, focused classification, and local refinement, we resolve intra-monomeric engagement of the biotin carboxyl carrier protein (BCCP) domain at both catalytic centers within the intact tetramer. Three-dimensional variability analysis reveals coordinated but non-synchronous hinge-centered domain motions that shift the population of accessible conformational states rather than enforcing a single active conformation. These findings provide structural insight into ensemble-based allosteric regulation and a species-specific quaternary architecture in a medically critical pathogen enzyme.
